questions.stem: Jess started work 20 years ago. In year 1 her annual salary was £17 000. Her annual salary increased by £1 500 each year, so that her annual salary in year 2 was £18 500, in year 3 it was £20 000 and so on, forming an arithmetic sequence. This continued until she reached her maximum annual salary of £32 000 in year $k$. Her annual salary then remained at £32 000.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of the constant $k$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $32000$ with a correct formula in an attempt to find $k$. A correct formula could be implied by a correct answer: $32000=17000+(k-1)\times 1500\Rightarrow k=\ldots$
A1: $(k=)11$ cso (Allow $n=11$). Accept correct answer only. $32000=17000+1500k\Rightarrow k=10$ is M0A0 (wrong formula). $\frac{32000-17000}{1500}=10\therefore k=11$ is M1A1 (correct formula implied). Listing: All terms must be listed up to 32000 and 11 correctly identified. A solution that scores 2 if fully correct and 0 otherwise.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Calculate the total amount that Jess has earned in the 20 years.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of correct sum formula with their integer $n=k$ or $k-1$ from part (a) where $3<k<20$ and $a=17000$ and $d=1500$: $S=\frac{k}{2}(2\times 17000+(k-1)\times 1500)$ or $\frac{k}{2}(17000+32000)$ or $S=\frac{k-1}{2}(2\times 17000+(k-2)\times 1500)$ or $\frac{k-1}{2}(17000+30500)$
A1: Any correct un-simplified numerical expression with $n=11$ or $n=10$: $S=\frac{11}{2}(2\times 17000+10\times 1500)$ or $\frac{11}{2}(17000+32000)$ or $S=\frac{10}{2}(2\times 17000+9\times 1500)$ or $\frac{10}{2}(17000+30500)$ ($=269500$ or $237500$)
M1: $32000\times\alpha$ where $\alpha$ is an integer and $3<\alpha<18$
ddM1: Attempts to add their two values. Dependent upon the two previous M's being scored and must be the sum of 20 terms i.e. $\alpha+k=20$: $288000+269500=557500$ or $320000+237500=557500$
A1: $557500$
Special Case: If they just find $S_{20}$ (£625000) in (b) score the first M1 otherwise apply the scheme.
Listing table (n=1..20, $u_n$: 17000,18500,20000,21500,23000,24500,26000,27500,29000,30500,32000,32000,32000,32000,32000,32000,32000,32000,32000,32000). Look for a sum before awarding marks. Award the M's as above then A2 for 557500. If they sum the 'parts' separately then apply the scheme.

questions.stem:
A curve with equation $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$ passes through the point $(4, 9)$.
Given that
$\mathrm{f}'(x)=\dfrac{3\sqrt{x}}{2}-\dfrac{9}{4\sqrt{x}}+2$, $x>0$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find $\mathrm{f}(x)$, giving each term in its simplest form.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $x^n\to x^{n+1}$
A1: Two terms in $x$ correct, simplification is not required in coefficients or powers: $\mathrm{f}(x)=x^{3/2}-\frac{9}{2}x^{1/2}+2x(+c)$

M1: Sub $x=4, y=9$ into $\mathrm{f}(x)\Rightarrow c=\ldots$. If no $+c$ then M0. Use of $x=9, y=4$ is M0.
A1: $(\mathrm{f}(x)=)x^{3/2}-\frac{9}{2}x^{1/2}+2x+2$. Accept equivalents but must be simplified e.g. $\mathrm{f}(x)=x^{3/2}-4.5\sqrt{x}+2x+2$. Must be all 'on one line' and simplified. Allow $x\sqrt{x}$ for $x^{3/2}$.

parts.label: b

The normal to the curve at $P$ is parallel to the line $2y+x=0$
(b) Find the $x$ coordinate of $P$.
(5)

A1: $x=1.5$ ($\frac{3}{2}$) Accept equivalents e.g. $x=\frac{9}{6}$. If any 'extra' values are not rejected, score A0.
